title: Grateful Dead Live at Public Hall on 1973-12-06

ai_review.summary: High‑energy ’73 show with a monster Here Comes Sunshine and long Dark Star captured on a clean soundboard upgrade
ai_review.review: Fans rave about the historic second set – a 20‑minute Here Comes Sunshine, an expansive Dark Star > Eyes > Stella Blue sequence and a superb Big River – while noting that the first set is uneven but still solid. The Miller SBD upgrade delivers clear, well‑balanced soundboard audio; the only technical quibble is a missing ~20‑second intro to Dark Star on this particular file.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews are 5‑star, praising the musical performance and describing the soundboard as a clear upgrade; only a few minor criticisms (missing intro, some flat first‑set songs) keep the rating from perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, well‑balanced SBD with an upgrade over earlier releases; minor issue – ~20 s of Dark Star intro missing and occasional track‑timing quirks.

poor_songs: Beat It On Down The Line (meh)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is a mixed bag – strong early numbers, some average moments, but builds into a solid second set anchored by the epic Here Comes Sunshine and Dark Star. Transitions are fluid and the band stretches out nicely.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for wailing guitar tone on HCS, Dark Star, and overall solo work; noted as "smoking" and "fine singing".
band_member_comments.Phil: Described as "smoldering", "fuzz‑tone bass" and providing a powerful underpinning throughout the long jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Commentary during the show is highlighted; his rhythm guitar and vocal contributions are mentioned but not singled out for performance quality.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith (keyboard) gets kudos for nice piano on Big River, switching to Rhodes during Dark Star, and overall solid support.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill (drums) noted as “beats his drum kit to death” on Big River; generally regarded as driving the groove.
